facts.assertion: GLA defines a Site Allocation as a site allocated for a particular type of development or use within a development plan.
GLA says allocated sites provide guidelines for planning decisions and promote development at borough level.
GLA states Site Allocation GIS boundaries are indicative and the relevant London Borough should be contacted to confirm accuracy.
GLA publishes a 5.11 MB Site Allocations GeoPackage in EPSG:27700 British National Grid.
The GLA Site Allocations dataset is licensed under Open Government Licence v3.0.
GLA identifies GLA Planning as maintainer of the Site Allocations dataset.
GLA identifies Custom Polygons as the smallest geography for Site Allocations.
Planning Data documents latitude plus longitude queries as returning entities whose geometry intersects the constructed point.
Planning Data requires both latitude and longitude for point-geometry intersection searching.
Planning Data allows multiple dataset parameters in a coordinate query.
Planning Data documents WKT geometry queries with selectable geometry relations including intersects.
Planning Data says coordinate geometry should be WGS84 EPSG:4326.
Planning Data supports offset-based pagination for large result sets.
Planning Data responses include pre-built next, previous, first and last pagination links.
Planning Data says its API has no batch endpoint and recommends one request per property for portfolio screening.
Planning Data recommends bulk downloads for hundreds of properties or more.
Planning Data warns that absence of API results does not prove no planning constraints exist because dataset coverage varies by area.
This continuation's direct parameterised GLA candidate-point URLs were rejected by the web client as unsafe to open, so no result was obtained.
A failed or unexecuted parameterised query is neither positive nor negative parcel-membership evidence.
Business scoring remains fail-closed until a candidate point is bound by executed authoritative geometry or equivalent complete-geometry evidence.
